mechanism_of_action: Increase cholinergic (ACh) signaling at muscarinic and/or nicotinic receptors (direct agonists) or by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase (indirect).
indications: Urinary retention; GI hypomotility; glaucoma; xerostomia; myasthenia gravis; reversal of non-depolarizing neuromuscular blockade; antimuscarinic toxicity (specific).
adverse_effects_common: Sweating; salivation; lacrimation; miosis; abdominal cramps; diarrhea; bronchial secretions.
adverse_effects_serious: Bronchospasm; severe bradycardia/AV block; hypotension; cholinergic crisis; seizures (some AChE inhibitors).
interactions_key: Additive bradycardia with beta blockers; antagonized by antimuscarinics; AChE inhibitors interact with depolarizing/non-depolarizing NMBs.
routes: PO; SC; IV; IM; ophthalmic; inhalation
notes: Core toxidrome: DUMBBELS/SLUDGE; treat severe muscarinic effects with atropine; consider pralidoxime for organophosphate poisoning.

mechanism_of_action: Direct muscarinic agonist (M3>M2) increases detrusor contraction and GI motility.
indications: Postoperative/postpartum urinary retention; neurogenic bladder; ileus.
contraindications: Mechanical urinary or GI obstruction; asthma; peptic ulcer disease; bradycardia/hypotension.
adverse_effects_common: Flushing; sweating; salivation; abdominal cramps; diarrhea; urinary urgency.
interactions_key: Additive bradycardia with beta blockers; antagonized by atropine/antimuscarinics.

mechanism_of_action: Direct muscarinic agonist (M3) increases exocrine secretion and causes miosis.
contraindications: Uncontrolled asthma/COPD; acute iritis/uveitis (caution); cardiovascular instability (caution).
adverse_effects_common: Sweating; salivation; nausea; rhinitis; urinary frequency; blurred vision.
interactions_key: Additive cholinergic effects with AChE inhibitors; antagonized by antimuscarinics.
notes: Can precipitate bronchospasm in susceptible patients.

mechanism_of_action: Direct muscarinic agonist (M3-selective) increases salivary secretion.
contraindications: Uncontrolled asthma; narrow-angle glaucoma (caution); significant cardiac conduction disease (caution).
adverse_effects_common: Sweating; nausea; rhinitis; diarrhea; visual disturbances.
interactions_key: Additive cholinergic effects with AChE inhibitors; antagonized by antimuscarinics.
notes: Prefer M3 selectivity vs pilocarpine (still systemic cholinergic AEs).

mechanism_of_action: Direct muscarinic agonist used to provoke bronchoconstriction.
contraindications: Asthma with severe obstruction; uncontrolled hypertension; recent MI/stroke; aortic aneurysm.
interactions_key: Beta blockers may blunt rescue bronchodilation; antagonized by inhaled beta-2 agonists.
notes: Diagnostic agent, not therapy; ensure bronchodilator rescue available.

mechanism_of_action: Direct muscarinic agonist (also nicotinic) causes miosis and ↑aqueous outflow.
interactions_key: Additive with other cholinergics; antagonized by antimuscarinics.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibit acetylcholinesterase, increasing ACh at synapses and NMJ (reversible agents) or irreversibly (organophosphates).
indications: Myasthenia gravis; reversal of non-depolarizing neuromuscular blockade; ileus/urinary retention (selected); antimuscarinic toxicity (physostigmine).
contraindications: Mechanical GI/GU obstruction; asthma/COPD (caution); bradyarrhythmias; seizures (caution).
adverse_effects_common: Cholinergic excess: diarrhea; urination; miosis; bronchial secretions; bradycardia.
adverse_effects_serious: Cholinergic crisis; bronchospasm; severe bradycardia/AV block; seizures (especially CNS-penetrant).
interactions_key: Additive bradycardia with beta blockers; antagonized by atropine; affects response to neuromuscular blockers.
notes: Separate muscarinic effects (treat with atropine) from nicotinic weakness (manage airway; pralidoxime for organophosphates).

mechanism_of_action: Reversible AChE inhibitor (quaternary, peripheral) ↑ACh at NMJ and parasympathetic sites.
indications: Reversal of non-depolarizing neuromuscular blockade; myasthenia gravis; postoperative ileus/urinary retention (selected).
contraindications: Mechanical GI/GU obstruction; peritonitis; asthma/COPD (caution); bradyarrhythmias.
adverse_effects_serious: Bronchospasm; severe bradycardia/AV block; cholinergic crisis.
interactions_key: Given with antimuscarinic (glycopyrrolate/atropine) for NMB reversal; additive bradycardia with beta blockers.

mechanism_of_action: Reversible AChE inhibitor (quaternary, peripheral) ↑ACh at NMJ.
interactions_key: Additive bradycardia with beta blockers; antagonized by antimuscarinics for muscarinic effects.
notes: Longer acting than neostigmine; titrate to avoid cholinergic crisis.

mechanism_of_action: Reversible AChE inhibitor (tertiary, crosses BBB) reverses central and peripheral antimuscarinic toxicity.
contraindications: TCA overdose (risk arrhythmias); conduction defects; asthma/COPD (caution).
interactions_key: Avoid with drugs causing conduction delay (e.g., TCAs); additive bradycardia with beta blockers.
notes: Use slow IV with monitoring; have atropine ready.

mechanism_of_action: Short-acting reversible AChE inhibitor.
indications: Historic/rare: diagnostic test in myasthenia gravis; reversal of NMB (limited).
interactions_key: Additive bradycardia with beta blockers; antagonized by atropine.
notes: Mostly replaced by better diagnostics; include for completeness.

mechanism_of_action: Competitive antagonists at muscarinic receptors; reduce parasympathetic tone (secretions, bronchoconstriction, GI motility, bladder contraction) and can cause mydriasis/tachycardia.
indications: Bradycardia; organophosphate poisoning (adjunct); COPD/asthma (inhaled); overactive bladder; motion sickness; GI spasm; preoperative secretion reduction; Parkinson tremor (selected).
contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma; urinary retention/BPH; ileus; myasthenia gravis (caution, except for specific uses).
adverse_effects_common: Dry mouth; blurred vision; constipation; urinary retention; tachycardia.
adverse_effects_serious: Hyperthermia; acute angle-closure glaucoma; severe urinary retention; delirium (elderly).
interactions_key: Additive anticholinergic burden with TCAs/antipsychotics/1st gen antihistamines; reduces GI absorption of some drugs; caution with dementia meds (AChEIs).
routes: PO; IV; IM; inhalation; ophthalmic; transdermal
notes: Classic toxidrome: hot as a hare, dry as a bone, blind as a bat, mad as a hatter; physostigmine can reverse severe central toxicity in selected cases.

mechanism_of_action: Competitive muscarinic antagonist; increases HR; reduces secretions; bronchodilation.
indications: Symptomatic bradycardia; organophosphate poisoning (with pralidoxime); preop secretion reduction.
contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma; urinary retention; ileus; tachyarrhythmias (caution).
adverse_effects_common: Dry mouth; blurred vision; tachycardia; constipation.
interactions_key: Additive anticholinergic effects; caution with other tachycardic agents.
notes: Primary antidote for muscarinic symptoms in cholinesterase inhibitor poisoning.

mechanism_of_action: Muscarinic antagonist (CNS-penetrant) reduces vestibular signaling.
contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma; urinary retention; delirium risk (elderly).

mechanism_of_action: Inhaled muscarinic antagonist (M3) bronchodilation; minimal systemic absorption.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity; narrow-angle glaucoma (nebulized mist contact risk).
adverse_effects_serious: Paradoxical bronchospasm (rare); acute glaucoma if aerosol into eyes.

mechanism_of_action: Long-acting inhaled muscarinic antagonist (LAMA) bronchodilation.
Quaternary antimuscarinic reduces secretions; minimal CNS effects.
indications: Preop secretion reduction; with neostigmine for NMB reversal; drooling (selected).
notes: Preferred over atropine when avoiding CNS effects.

mechanism_of_action: Antimuscarinic (M3) decreases detrusor overactivity.
contraindications: Urinary retention; gastric retention/ileus; narrow-angle glaucoma.
interactions_key: Additive anticholinergic effects; CYP interactions vary by formulation.
notes: High anticholinergic burden vs newer agents.

mechanism_of_action: Antimuscarinic for OAB (more bladder-selective than oxybutynin).
contraindications: Urinary retention; gastric retention; narrow-angle glaucoma.
interactions_key: CYP3A4 inhibitors can increase levels (some formulations).

mechanism_of_action: M3-selective antimuscarinic for OAB.
contraindications: Urinary retention; gastric retention; narrow-angle glaucoma.
interactions_key: CYP3A4 inhibitors increase exposure; additive QT risk with other QT-prolonging drugs.

mechanism_of_action: Quaternary antimuscarinic for OAB (less CNS penetration).
contraindications: Urinary retention; gastric retention; narrow-angle glaucoma.
interactions_key: Additive anticholinergic burden; separate from high-fat meals (absorption).
notes: Lower CNS effects due to quaternary structure.

mechanism_of_action: Central antimuscarinic (also antihistamine) improves Parkinson tremor and drug-induced EPS.
indications: Parkinson disease tremor; antipsychotic-induced extrapyramidal symptoms.
contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma; urinary retention; ileus; dementia (caution).
adverse_effects_common: Dry mouth; constipation; blurred vision; confusion.
interactions_key: Additive anticholinergic effects; avoid with other strong anticholinergics.
notes: Use lowest effective dose, especially elderly.

mechanism_of_action: Central antimuscarinic for Parkinson tremor/EPS.
contraindications: Narrow-angle glaucoma; urinary retention; ileus; dementia (caution).

mechanism_of_action: Antimuscarinic reduces GI smooth muscle spasm.
contraindications: Infants; ileus; myasthenia gravis; glaucoma; urinary retention.
notes: Avoid in infants; anticholinergic toxicity risk.

mechanism_of_action: Stimulate adrenergic receptors (α/β) directly or increase synaptic catecholamines indirectly, producing vasoconstriction, bronchodilation, and/or cardiac stimulation.
indications: Anaphylaxis; shock; cardiac arrest; bradycardia; asthma/COPD; nasal congestion; hypotension; preterm labor (selected).
contraindications: Severe tachyarrhythmias; uncontrolled hypertension; ischemic heart disease (caution); hyperthyroidism (caution).
adverse_effects_serious: Arrhythmias; myocardial ischemia; severe hypertension; stroke.
interactions_key: MAO inhibitors/TCAs increase effects; beta blockers can cause unopposed α (nonselective); additive QT/arrhythmia risk with other sympathomimetics.
routes: IV; IM; SC; inhalation; intranasal; ophthalmic; PO
notes: Know receptor profiles: α1 vasoconstriction; β1 cardiac; β2 bronchodilation/tocolysis; α2 central sympatholysis (sometimes taught separately).

mechanism_of_action: Nonselective α1/α2/β1/β2 agonist; dose-dependent β then α effects.
indications: Anaphylaxis (IM); cardiac arrest; severe asthma; vasopressor support (selected).
contraindications: No absolute CI in anaphylaxis; otherwise: severe arrhythmias, uncontrolled hypertension (caution).
interactions_key: MAOIs/TCAs potentiate; nonselective beta blockers increase hypertension risk; avoid mixing with certain anesthetics (arrhythmia risk).

mechanism_of_action: α1/α2 strong, β1 moderate agonist; potent vasoconstrictor.
adverse_effects_common: Tachycardia (less than dopamine); headache; extravasation injury.
interactions_key: MAOIs/TCAs potentiate; avoid with ergot alkaloids; requires central line ideally.
notes: Use with adequate volume; monitor perfusion.

mechanism_of_action: Dose-dependent: D1 (renal) -> β1 -> α1 at higher doses.
indications: Shock with bradycardia (selected); HF with hypotension (selected).
interactions_key: MAOIs increase effects; halogenated anesthetics increase arrhythmia risk.
notes: Use has decreased vs norepinephrine in many protocols.

mechanism_of_action: Predominantly β1 agonist (some β2/α1); increases inotropy more than HR.
indications: Acute decompensated HF/cardiogenic shock (inotrope); stress echocardiography.
interactions_key: Additive arrhythmias with other sympathomimetics; beta blockers blunt effect.
notes: Improves cardiac output; may lower SVR slightly.

mechanism_of_action: Nonselective β1/β2 agonist; strong chronotrope/inotrope; vasodilates.
notes: Can cause hypotension due to β2 vasodilation.

mechanism_of_action: Selective α1 agonist causes vasoconstriction.
contraindications: Severe hypertension; ventricular tachycardia; narrow-angle glaucoma (topical caution).
interactions_key: MAOIs/TCAs potentiate; avoid with other vasoconstrictors.

mechanism_of_action: Prodrug to α1 agonist; increases peripheral vascular resistance.
contraindications: Severe organic heart disease; acute renal disease; urinary retention; supine hypertension.
interactions_key: Additive hypertension with other pressors; caution with beta blockers (bradycardia).
notes: Avoid dosing near bedtime to reduce supine HTN.

mechanism_of_action: Topical α agonist causes nasal mucosal vasoconstriction.
adverse_effects_serious: Rebound congestion with overuse; hypertension (rare systemic).
notes: Limit to 3 days to avoid rebound.

mechanism_of_action: Indirect/weak direct sympathomimetic; decongestant.
contraindications: Severe hypertension; CAD; hyperthyroidism; glaucoma; BPH (caution).
interactions_key: MAOIs contraindicated; additive with other stimulants.
notes: Abuse potential; restrictions in many countries.

mechanism_of_action: Selective β2 agonist bronchodilator.
interactions_key: Nonselective beta blockers antagonize; additive hypokalemia with diuretics.

mechanism_of_action: β2 agonist bronchodilator; also uterine relaxation.
interactions_key: Additive with other sympathomimetics; beta blockers antagonize.

mechanism_of_action: Long-acting β2 agonist (LABA) bronchodilator.
indications: COPD maintenance; asthma (only with inhaled corticosteroid).
adverse_effects_serious: Asthma-related death if used without ICS; arrhythmias (rare).
interactions_key: Beta blockers antagonize; additive sympathomimetic effects.
notes: LABA: always pair with ICS in asthma.

mechanism_of_action: LABA with relatively fast onset; bronchodilator.
β3 agonist relaxes detrusor muscle, increasing bladder capacity.
contraindications: Severe uncontrolled hypertension; bladder outlet obstruction (caution).
interactions_key: CYP2D6 inhibitor can increase levels of some drugs (e.g., metoprolol).
notes: Useful when anticholinergic burden is a problem.

mechanism_of_action: Reduce sympathetic activity via α/β receptor antagonism, central α2 agonism, inhibition of catecholamine release, or synthesis blockade.
indications: Hypertension; angina; arrhythmias; heart failure (selected beta blockers); BPH (α1 blockers); pheochromocytoma (α blockade).
contraindications: Bradycardia/AV block; severe asthma (nonselective β blockers); cardiogenic shock (relative); severe hypotension.
adverse_effects_serious: Severe bradycardia/heart block; bronchospasm; heart failure decompensation; severe hypotension; rebound hypertension (central agents).
interactions_key: Additive hypotension with other antihypertensives; β blockers with verapamil/diltiazem → AV block; central α2 agonists + CNS depressants.
notes: Split into: α blockers; β blockers; mixed α/β; central α2 agonists; others (rare).

mechanism_of_action: Selective α1 blocker → vasodilation; ↓afterload.
interactions_key: Additive hypotension with PDE5 inhibitors and other antihypertensives.
notes: Give first dose at bedtime to reduce syncope risk.

mechanism_of_action: Selective α1 blocker → vasodilation; relaxes prostate/bladder neck.
Selective α1 blocker for HTN/BPH.
Selective α1A blocker (prostate) improves urinary flow.
adverse_effects_serious: Intraoperative floppy iris syndrome (IFIS) in cataract surgery.
interactions_key: CYP3A4 inhibitors increase levels; additive hypotension with other agents.

mechanism_of_action: Irreversible nonselective α blocker.
adverse_effects_common: Orthostatic hypotension; nasal congestion; reflex tachycardia.
interactions_key: Additive hypotension; use beta blocker only after adequate alpha blockade.
notes: Always block α before β in pheochromocytoma to avoid hypertensive crisis.

mechanism_of_action: Reversible nonselective α blocker; rapid onset.
indications: Catecholamine-induced hypertensive emergencies; extravasation of vasopressors (local).
interactions_key: Additive hypotension; caution with beta blockers.

mechanism_of_action: Nonselective β1/β2 blocker; ↓HR/contractility; ↓renin.
indications: Hypertension; angina; essential tremor; migraine prophylaxis; thyrotoxicosis symptoms.
contraindications: Asthma/COPD; bradycardia; AV block; decompensated HF.
interactions_key: Additive AV block with verapamil/diltiazem; masks hypoglycemia with insulin; avoid abrupt withdrawal.

mechanism_of_action: Selective β1 blocker (dose-dependent).
adverse_effects_serious: Severe bradycardia; AV block; HF worsening.
interactions_key: CYP2D6 inhibitors increase levels; additive AV block with verapamil/diltiazem.
notes: β1 selectivity decreases bronchospasm risk (not zero).

mechanism_of_action: Selective β1 blocker.
interactions_key: Additive AV block with verapamil/diltiazem; avoid abrupt withdrawal.

mechanism_of_action: Selective β1 blocker; more hydrophilic.
notes: Less CNS penetration; some prefer alternatives in pregnancy.

mechanism_of_action: β1 blocker with NO-mediated vasodilation.
Nonselective β blocker + α1 blocker.
interactions_key: Additive hypotension with other antihypertensives; AV block with non-DHP CCBs.

mechanism_of_action: β blocker + α1 blocker; lowers BP without major HR increase.
interactions_key: Additive hypotension; AV block with non-DHP CCBs.

mechanism_of_action: Ultra–short acting β1 blocker (esterase metabolism).
interactions_key: Additive AV block with non-DHP CCBs.
notes: Good when you want rapid on/off.

mechanism_of_action: Nonselective β blocker (often ophthalmic).
interactions_key: Additive with other β blockers; caution with verapamil/diltiazem.
notes: Topical can still cause systemic β blockade.

mechanism_of_action: Nonselective β blocker + class III antiarrhythmic effects.
contraindications: QT prolongation; severe renal impairment (dose adjust).
interactions_key: Additive QT prolongation with other QT-prolonging drugs; electrolyte disturbances increase risk.

mechanism_of_action: Central α2 agonist decreases sympathetic outflow → ↓BP; also reduces withdrawal symptoms.
interactions_key: Additive CNS depression; beta blockers increase rebound risk if clonidine stopped first (taper).

mechanism_of_action: Converted to α-methylnorepinephrine (central α2 agonist) ↓sympathetic tone.
interactions_key: Additive with other antihypertensives; may interfere with Coombs testing.
notes: Historic first-line in pregnancy; still taught heavily.

mechanism_of_action: Central α2A agonist reduces sympathetic outflow; also used in ADHD.
interactions_key: Additive CNS depression; CYP3A4 interactions (some formulations).

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits tyrosine hydroxylase → ↓catecholamine synthesis.
interactions_key: Additive CNS depression; combine with α/β blockers as needed.
notes: Used as adjunct preop in pheochromocytoma.

mechanism_of_action: Blocks VMAT → depletes NE/DA/5-HT in nerve terminals.
interactions_key: Additive hypotension with other antihypertensives; avoid with MAOIs.

mechanism_of_action: Reduce gastric acid secretion, neutralize acid, or eradicate Helicobacter pylori.
indications: Peptic ulcer disease; GERD; stress ulcer prophylaxis; H. pylori eradication.
adverse_effects_serious: GI bleeding masking; infections with acid suppression.
interactions_key: PPIs reduce absorption of drugs needing acidic pH; cimetidine inhibits CYP.

mechanism_of_action: Irreversibly inhibits H+/K+ ATPase in parietal cells.
Irreversibly inhibits H+/K+ ATPase in parietal cells.
Irreversibly inhibits H+/K+ ATPase in parietal cells.
Irreversibly inhibits H+/K+ ATPase in parietal cells.

Coats ulcer; antimicrobial vs H. pylori.

Inhibits prostaglandin and leukotriene synthesis in gut.
Suppresses inflammatory gene transcription.

D2 antagonist; ↑ gastric emptying.

Increases stool water content or stimulates peristalsis.
Increases stool water content or stimulates peristalsis.
Peripheral μ-opioid receptor agonist ↓ gut motility.
notes: Does not cross BBB at therapeutic doses.

mechanism_of_action: Therapies affecting glucocorticoids, mineralocorticoids, adrenal steroid synthesis, and adrenal hormone antagonism.
indications: Adrenal insufficiency; congenital adrenal hyperplasia; Cushing syndrome; mineralocorticoid deficiency; hyperaldosteronism; adrenal crisis.
adverse_effects_common: Weight gain; fluid retention; mood changes (steroids).
adverse_effects_serious: Adrenal suppression; severe infections; GI bleeding; psychosis (steroids).
interactions_key: CYP3A4 inducers reduce steroid levels; additive hypokalemia with diuretics (some).

mechanism_of_action: Binds glucocorticoid receptor → alters gene transcription; anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive; metabolic effects.
indications: Adrenal insufficiency (hydrocortisone); inflammatory/autoimmune diseases; cerebral edema (dexamethasone); diagnostic suppression tests (dexamethasone).
contraindications: Systemic fungal infection (relative); live vaccines with high-dose therapy; severe uncontrolled infection (relative).
adverse_effects_common: Weight gain; hyperglycemia; mood changes; hypertension; insomnia.
adverse_effects_serious: Adrenal suppression; osteoporosis; GI bleeding; severe infection; psychosis; avascular necrosis (long-term).
interactions_key: CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors affect levels; NSAIDs ↑ GI bleed; vaccines (reduced response).
notes: Physiologic replacement and stress dosing; has mineralocorticoid activity.

mechanism_of_action: Binds glucocorticoid receptor → alters gene transcription; anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive; metabolic effects.
indications: Adrenal insufficiency (hydrocortisone); inflammatory/autoimmune diseases; cerebral edema (dexamethasone); diagnostic suppression tests (dexamethasone).
contraindications: Systemic fungal infection (relative); live vaccines with high-dose therapy; severe uncontrolled infection (relative).
adverse_effects_common: Weight gain; hyperglycemia; mood changes; hypertension; insomnia.
adverse_effects_serious: Adrenal suppression; osteoporosis; GI bleeding; severe infection; psychosis; avascular necrosis (long-term).
interactions_key: CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors affect levels; NSAIDs ↑ GI bleed; vaccines (reduced response).

mechanism_of_action: Binds glucocorticoid receptor → alters gene transcription; anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive; metabolic effects.
indications: Adrenal insufficiency (hydrocortisone); inflammatory/autoimmune diseases; cerebral edema (dexamethasone); diagnostic suppression tests (dexamethasone).
contraindications: Systemic fungal infection (relative); live vaccines with high-dose therapy; severe uncontrolled infection (relative).
adverse_effects_common: Weight gain; hyperglycemia; mood changes; hypertension; insomnia.
adverse_effects_serious: Adrenal suppression; osteoporosis; GI bleeding; severe infection; psychosis; avascular necrosis (long-term).
interactions_key: CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors affect levels; NSAIDs ↑ GI bleed; vaccines (reduced response).
notes: Long-acting potent glucocorticoid; minimal mineralocorticoid effect.

mechanism_of_action: Mineralocorticoid receptor agonist → ↑Na+ reabsorption and K+/H+ excretion in kidney.
indications: Primary adrenal insufficiency mineralocorticoid replacement; orthostatic hypotension (selected).
interactions_key: Additive hypokalemia with loop/thiazide diuretics; interacts with antihypertensives.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits adrenal and gonadal steroid synthesis (CYP enzymes).
Inhibits 11β-hydroxylase → ↓cortisol synthesis.
interactions_key: Additive with other adrenal inhibitors; affects cortisol assays.

mechanism_of_action: Cytotoxic to adrenal cortex; reduces steroid synthesis.
Antagonizes glucocorticoid receptor (also progesterone receptor).
Blocks mineralocorticoid receptor → ↓Na+ retention, ↑K+ retention; antifibrotic effects.
indications: Primary hyperaldosteronism; resistant hypertension; heart failure (selected).
contraindications: Hyperkalemia; severe renal impairment; Addison disease.
interactions_key: Additive hyperkalemia with ACEi/ARB/K+ supplements; NSAIDs ↓ renal function.
notes: Antiandrogen effects; useful for hyperaldosteronism and resistant HTN.

mechanism_of_action: Blocks mineralocorticoid receptor → ↓Na+ retention, ↑K+ retention; antifibrotic effects.
indications: Primary hyperaldosteronism; resistant hypertension; heart failure (selected).
contraindications: Hyperkalemia; severe renal impairment; Addison disease.
interactions_key: Additive hyperkalemia with ACEi/ARB/K+ supplements; NSAIDs ↓ renal function.
notes: More selective MR antagonist; fewer endocrine side effects.

mechanism_of_action: Therapies affecting estrogens, progestins, androgens, antiandrogens, and hormonal contraception.
indications: Contraception; menopausal symptoms; hypogonadism; endometriosis; PCOS; prostate cancer (selected).
contraindications: Estrogen-dependent tumors; history of thromboembolism (combined OCP); severe liver disease (agent-dependent).
interactions_key: Enzyme inducers reduce hormonal contraception efficacy; anticoagulants and VTE risk.
routes: PO; transdermal; IM; SC; IUD; implant
notes: Know absolute contraindications for combined estrogen-progestin contraception.

mechanism_of_action: Estrogen receptor agonist; suppresses FSH; stabilizes endometrium.
indications: Combined hormonal contraception; menopausal hormone therapy (in combination).
contraindications: History of VTE/stroke; estrogen-dependent cancer; severe liver disease; migraine with aura; smokers >35y.

mechanism_of_action: Progesterone receptor agonist; thickens cervical mucus; suppresses LH surge; alters endometrium.
contraindications: Active breast cancer; unexplained vaginal bleeding; severe liver disease (relative).
adverse_effects_common: Irregular bleeding; weight gain; mood changes.
adverse_effects_serious: Bone density loss (depot); thrombosis risk (lower than estrogen).
notes: Progestin used in OCPs and emergency contraception; also IUD.

mechanism_of_action: Progesterone receptor agonist; thickens cervical mucus; suppresses LH surge; alters endometrium.
contraindications: Active breast cancer; unexplained vaginal bleeding; severe liver disease (relative).
adverse_effects_common: Irregular bleeding; weight gain; mood changes.
adverse_effects_serious: Bone density loss (depot); thrombosis risk (lower than estrogen).
notes: Depot contraception; can decrease bone density with long-term use.

mechanism_of_action: Suppresses ovulation (↓FSH/LH); progestin thickens cervical mucus; endometrial changes.
indications: Contraception; dysmenorrhea; acne; PCOS symptom control (selected).
contraindications: VTE history; migraine with aura; smokers >35y; uncontrolled HTN; estrogen-dependent tumors; severe liver disease.
interactions_key: Enzyme inducers ↓ efficacy; rifampicin and some antiepileptics are high-risk.
notes: Counsel on VTE symptoms; adherence crucial.

mechanism_of_action: Androgen receptor agonist; supports male secondary sex characteristics; anabolic effects.
contraindications: Prostate/breast cancer; polycythemia; severe heart failure (caution).
interactions_key: Warfarin ↑ bleeding risk; insulin requirements may change.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits 5α-reductase → ↓DHT.
notes: Avoid handling crushed tablets in pregnancy.

mechanism_of_action: Weak androgen receptor antagonist; inhibits androgen synthesis; also MR antagonist.
Lower glucose via insulin replacement or agents improving insulin secretion/sensitivity or reducing glucose absorption/production.
indications: Type 1 diabetes; type 2 diabetes; diabetic emergencies (insulin).
adverse_effects_serious: Severe hypoglycemia; ketoacidosis (SGLT2, rare); lactic acidosis (metformin, rare).
interactions_key: Insulin + beta blockers mask hypoglycemia; metformin + contrast; sulfonylureas + alcohol.
notes: Document: hypoglycemia risk, weight effect, renal dosing.

mechanism_of_action: Insulin receptor agonist → ↑glucose uptake, ↓hepatic glucose output; shifts K+ into cells.
indications: Diabetes mellitus; DKA (regular insulin IV); hyperkalemia (adjunct).
contraindications: Hypoglycemia; cautious titration in renal impairment.
interactions_key: Beta blockers mask hypoglycemia symptoms; alcohol ↑ hypoglycemia; additive with other antidiabetics.

mechanism_of_action: Insulin receptor agonist → ↑glucose uptake, ↓hepatic glucose output; shifts K+ into cells.
indications: Diabetes mellitus; DKA (regular insulin IV); hyperkalemia (adjunct).
contraindications: Hypoglycemia; cautious titration in renal impairment.
interactions_key: Beta blockers mask hypoglycemia symptoms; alcohol ↑ hypoglycemia; additive with other antidiabetics.
notes: Only insulin used IV for DKA.

mechanism_of_action: Insulin receptor agonist → ↑glucose uptake, ↓hepatic glucose output; shifts K+ into cells.
indications: Diabetes mellitus; DKA (regular insulin IV); hyperkalemia (adjunct).
contraindications: Hypoglycemia; cautious titration in renal impairment.
interactions_key: Beta blockers mask hypoglycemia symptoms; alcohol ↑ hypoglycemia; additive with other antidiabetics.

mechanism_of_action: Insulin receptor agonist → ↑glucose uptake, ↓hepatic glucose output; shifts K+ into cells.
indications: Diabetes mellitus; DKA (regular insulin IV); hyperkalemia (adjunct).
contraindications: Hypoglycemia; cautious titration in renal impairment.
interactions_key: Beta blockers mask hypoglycemia symptoms; alcohol ↑ hypoglycemia; additive with other antidiabetics.

mechanism_of_action: Decreases hepatic gluconeogenesis; ↑insulin sensitivity; ↓intestinal glucose absorption.
contraindications: Severely reduced renal function; metabolic acidosis; unstable hypoxia.
interactions_key: Iodinated contrast (hold temporarily); alcohol ↑ lactic acidosis risk.
notes: Weight neutral/weight loss; no hypoglycemia alone.

mechanism_of_action: Closes β-cell KATP channels → ↑insulin secretion.
contraindications: Type 1 diabetes; severe hepatic impairment; sulfa allergy (caution).
interactions_key: Alcohol ↑ hypoglycemia; many CYP interactions possible.
notes: Higher hypoglycemia risk, especially elderly/renal impairment.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits DPP-4 → ↑endogenous incretins → ↑insulin, ↓glucagon (glucose-dependent).
contraindications: History of pancreatitis (caution); renal dose adjust.

mechanism_of_action: GLP-1 receptor agonist → ↑insulin, ↓glucagon (glucose-dependent), slows gastric emptying, ↑satiety.
interactions_key: Slows gastric emptying affects absorption; with insulin/sulfonylureas ↑ hypoglycemia risk.
notes: Weight loss benefit; counsel GI effects.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits SGLT2 in proximal tubule → ↑urinary glucose excretion; osmotic diuresis.
adverse_effects_common: Genital mycotic infections; polyuria; volume depletion.
notes: Hold during acute illness/fasting/surgery to reduce DKA risk.

mechanism_of_action: Agents replacing or modulating pituitary hormones and controlling thyroid hormone synthesis or action.
indications: Hypothyroidism; hyperthyroidism; thyroid storm; acromegaly; diabetes insipidus; infertility (selected).
interactions_key: Levothyroxine interacts with warfarin; absorption reduced by iron/calcium; iodine timing with thionamides.
notes: High-yield: levothyroxine; methimazole/PTU; iodide; beta blockers; desmopressin; somatostatin analogs.

mechanism_of_action: Synthetic T4 → converted to T3; binds nuclear thyroid receptors.
interactions_key: Warfarin effect ↑; absorption reduced by iron/calcium; PPIs can alter absorption.
notes: Take on empty stomach; titrate by TSH.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits thyroid peroxidase → ↓organification and coupling (↓T3/T4 synthesis).
interactions_key: Warfarin dose adjustment as thyroid status changes.
notes: Check CBC if fever/sore throat; LFTs if symptoms.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibits thyroid peroxidase and peripheral conversion of T4→T3.
indications: Hyperthyroidism in 1st trimester pregnancy; thyroid storm.
interactions_key: Warfarin adjustment as thyroid status changes.

mechanism_of_action: Acute high-dose iodide inhibits thyroid hormone release and organification (Wolff–Chaikoff).
indications: Thyroid storm (after thionamide); preop preparation in Graves.
interactions_key: Give after thionamide to avoid iodine-as-substrate; interacts with lithium/amiodarone.

mechanism_of_action: β blockade reduces adrenergic symptoms; at high doses decreases T4→T3 conversion.
notes: Symptom control while waiting for definitive therapy.

mechanism_of_action: V2 receptor agonist → ↑water reabsorption; ↑vWF release.
indications: Central diabetes insipidus; nocturnal enuresis; von Willebrand disease (selected).
interactions_key: SSRIs/TCAs and others ↑ hyponatremia risk; monitor fluids.

mechanism_of_action: Somatostatin receptor agonist → ↓GH, ↓TSH, ↓GI hormone secretion.
interactions_key: May alter insulin needs; additive bradycardia with beta blockers.

mechanism_of_action: Cytotoxic agents that kill rapidly dividing cells via DNA damage, inhibition of DNA synthesis, or disruption of mitosis.
indications: Solid tumors and hematologic malignancies; adjuvant/neoadjuvant therapy; palliative regimens.
contraindications: Pregnancy (many agents); severe bone marrow suppression; active severe infection (relative); agent-dependent.
adverse_effects_serious: Febrile neutropenia/sepsis; severe bleeding; organ-specific toxicities (cardio/neuro/pulmonary/renal).
interactions_key: Live vaccines contraindicated during profound immunosuppression; additive myelosuppression; CYP interactions agent-dependent.
notes: Classic rule: dose-limiting toxicity is often myelosuppression, except where organ-specific toxicity dominates.

mechanism_of_action: Covalently alkylate DNA → crosslinking and strand breaks (cell cycle–nonspecific).
indications: Various cancers depending on agent and regimen.
adverse_effects_serious: Febrile neutropenia; secondary malignancy (some); organ toxicities (agent-specific).
interactions_key: Additive myelosuppression with other cytotoxics; CYP interactions agent-dependent.
notes: Includes cyclophosphamide/ifosfamide; risk hemorrhagic cystitis (acrolein) mitigated with MESNA (esp. ifosfamide).

mechanism_of_action: Form DNA crosslinks similar to alkylators; cell cycle–nonspecific.
indications: Various cancers depending on agent and regimen.
adverse_effects_serious: Febrile neutropenia; secondary malignancy (some); organ toxicities (agent-specific).
interactions_key: Additive myelosuppression with other cytotoxics; CYP interactions agent-dependent.
notes: Cisplatin: nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity; carboplatin: more myelosuppression; oxaliplatin: neuropathy (cold-induced).

mechanism_of_action: Inhibit DNA/RNA synthesis by mimicking folate/purines/pyrimidines (S-phase).
indications: Various cancers depending on agent and regimen.
adverse_effects_serious: Febrile neutropenia; secondary malignancy (some); organ toxicities (agent-specific).
interactions_key: Additive myelosuppression with other cytotoxics; CYP interactions agent-dependent.
notes: High-yield: methotrexate (rescue with leucovorin), 5-FU/capecitabine, cytarabine, gemcitabine.

mechanism_of_action: Intercalate DNA and/or generate free radicals; inhibit topoisomerase II (anthracyclines).
indications: Various cancers depending on agent and regimen.
adverse_effects_serious: Febrile neutropenia; secondary malignancy (some); organ toxicities (agent-specific).
interactions_key: Additive myelosuppression with other cytotoxics; CYP interactions agent-dependent.
notes: Doxorubicin: cardiomyopathy (dexrazoxane protective); bleomycin: pulmonary fibrosis; dactinomycin: severe mucositis.

mechanism_of_action: Inhibit topoisomerase I or II → DNA breaks during replication/repair.
indications: Various cancers depending on agent and regimen.
adverse_effects_serious: Febrile neutropenia; secondary malignancy (some); organ toxicities (agent-specific).
interactions_key: Additive myelosuppression with other cytotoxics; CYP interactions agent-dependent.
notes: Etoposide (Topo II): secondary leukemia risk; irinotecan/topotecan (Topo I): diarrhea/myelosuppression.

mechanism_of_action: Disrupt microtubule dynamics → mitotic arrest (M-phase).
indications: Various cancers depending on agent and regimen.
adverse_effects_serious: Febrile neutropenia; secondary malignancy (some); organ toxicities (agent-specific).
interactions_key: Additive myelosuppression with other cytotoxics; CYP interactions agent-dependent.
notes: Vinca alkaloids: neuropathy/ileus; taxanes: neuropathy, myelosuppression, hypersensitivity.

mechanism_of_action: Prodrug; alkylates DNA after hepatic activation → crosslinks.
indications: Lymphomas, leukemias, breast cancer, sarcomas; conditioning regimens; autoimmune (selected).
contraindications: Severe marrow suppression; active severe infection (relative); pregnancy.
adverse_effects_serious: Hemorrhagic cystitis; SIADH; secondary malignancy; cardiotoxicity (high-dose).
interactions_key: Additive myelosuppression; CYP inducers/inhibitors affect activation; avoid live vaccines.
notes: Hydration; consider MESNA in high-dose settings.

mechanism_of_action: Alkylates DNA (prodrug) → crosslinks; produces acrolein and chloroacetaldehyde.
contraindications: Severe marrow suppression; renal impairment (caution); pregnancy.
interactions_key: Additive CNS depressants (encephalopathy risk); avoid live vaccines; CYP interactions.

mechanism_of_action: Alkylates DNA; strong myeloablative effect.
notes: Seizure prophylaxis often used in conditioning protocols.

mechanism_of_action: Forms DNA crosslinks → apoptosis.
indications: Testicular, ovarian, bladder, lung cancers; many solid tumors.
adverse_effects_serious: Nephrotoxicity; ototoxicity; peripheral neuropathy; severe electrolyte wasting (Mg/K).
interactions_key: Additive nephrotoxicity with aminoglycosides/NSAIDs; avoid other ototoxins.

mechanism_of_action: DNA crosslinks; less nephro/oto than cisplatin.
indications: Ovarian and lung cancers; many solid tumors.
interactions_key: Additive myelosuppression; dose by renal function (Calvert formula).

mechanism_of_action: DNA crosslinks; distinct neurotoxicity profile.
interactions_key: Additive neurotoxicity with other neurotoxic agents.
notes: Avoid cold exposure around infusion to reduce acute neuropathy.

contraindications: Pregnancy; severe liver disease; significant renal impairment; active infection Dolphin?
interactions_key: NSAIDs, TMP-SMX, penicillins can ↑ toxicity; leucovorin rescue for high-dose.

mechanism_of_action: Pyrimidine analog; inhibits thymidylate synthase and incorporates into RNA/DNA.
